title: decommission-compat-beacons-and-compact-rollout-history
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Over the last three years we introduced several backward-compatibility mechanisms (compatibility beacons, legacy admin endpoints, and per-deployment rollout fingerprints) to support gradual rollouts and third-party integrators. Those adapters grew organic state in the rollout history table, produced duplicate flag translations, and are now a recurring source of latency and maintenance overhead for the runtime and admin query paths. Several recent incidents involved slow reads on the rollout history index and flaky canonicalization of flag keys during canary rollouts.

Goal: Remove the runtime compatibility beacons and legacy admin endpoints that perform on-the-fly flag translation, then compact and canonicalize rollout history into a normalized manifest. This reduces DB footprint, simplifies the runtime config surface, and improves rollout query latencies.

Scope:
- Stop writes to compat_beacons and deprecate the beacon handler.
- Migrate the rollout_history table: collapse historical variants to canonical manifest entries and emit a reconciliation report.
- Remove legacy admin endpoints that rely on the on-the-fly translation shim; replace callers with the new canonical route manifest API.
- Provide migration scripts, a runbook, and a short compatibility layer for external integrators with a 3-month grace period.

Out of scope: Removing flag UI or design-side migrations; deep GC of other audit logs (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: compat_beacons table is marked read-only and no upstream writes occur for >=48h in staging and >=7d in prod canary before deletion
rollout_history compacted: number of distinct manifest fingerprints reduced by >=90% for affected deployments
legacy admin endpoints return 410 and provide Location header linking to canonical manifest API after rollout window
runtime SLOs: admin query p99 latency improved by >=15% in canary region after change
migration scripts and runbook live in infra/migrations and Confluence; QA runbook executed in staging with test plan passing
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Spike completed — identified primary sources writing to compat_beacons (legacy rollout controller + two external integrators). Estimated data shape and size for migration: ~1.2M rows, 45GB indexed.
2025-01-22: Migration prototype (python ETL) created — compacts fingerprint groups and emits mapping file. Smoke tests in dev passed with synthetic data.
2025-01-30: Design review with PM and Security — agreed on 3-month grace period and deprecation headers. Security: no secret material stored in beacon rows.
2025-02-04: PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7128) with migration scripts and read-only DB trigger. Waiting on infra review.
2025-02-11: Infra approved scheduling window; canary region selected (us-west-2). Begin scheduling canary migration for 2025-02-20.
decisions: Perform an offline compaction (ETL) instead of in-place SQL deletes to avoid long locks on the rollout_history index.
Preserve a mapping file (legacy_key -> canonical_manifest_id) for the 3-month grace period rather than runtime translation to simplify runtime logic.
Expose deprecation via 410 + Location header on legacy admin endpoints to encourage programmatic migration and reduce human support load.
Rollout in canary (one region) then global after 7 days of stable metrics; use feature flag gating for immediate rollback.
testing_and_rollout_notes: Staging: run migration ETL against snapshot and validate compacted manifest matches pre-rollout behavior for 1000 sampled deployments.
Canary: select small subset of customers (<=5) in us-west-2 to run compaction and switch admin endpoints; monitor admin p99 and error rates for 7 days.
Rollback: keep mapping file and a read-only replica of compat_beacons for 14 days after canary; have manual restore documented if compaction leads to data loss.
Post-migration: schedule background job to delete compat_beacons rows after 90 days and update runbook to remove shim references.
